next_event.source: Lexical search for 'investor day' across FY2026 FND documents found no announcement; last Investor Day in corpus is 2022 (document_id 18784). No Item 2.01 or 1.01 8-K since 2024-07-01

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Long-term goal with no year. Wording has drifted: mid-teens target (2019), high teens (2022 Investor Day), mid- to high teens (Q1 FY2024), mid-teens (Q2 FY2025, Paulsen as President). Target taken as 15%. Not found restated in the Q1 or Q2 FY2026 calls since Paulsen became CEO. FY2026 guide: adj. EBITDA $550M to $585M on sales $4,770M to $4,990M (53-week year). Earliest statement found: Q4 FY2019 call (document_id 5615, mid-teens long-term target with 15 to 30 bps a year); exact call date not fetched, so first_stated is null.

statements.quote: So I mean there's a lot that we're doing internal to do that, and we'll keep a focus on cost as well. So longer term, we still believe in that goal of mid-teens EBITDA. That's -- we're still on that path.
statements.speaker: Bradley S. Paulsen
statements.doc_title: Floor & Decor Q2 FY2025 Earnings Call

statements.quote: We still see a path to achieving our long-term goal of mid- to high teens adjusted EBITDA margin.
statements.speaker: Bryan Langley
statements.doc_title: Floor & Decor Q1 FY2024 Earnings Call

statements.quote: Our second quarter adjusted EBITDA margin was 12.2%, compared with 12.4% in the prior year period.
statements.speaker: Bryan Langley

statements.quote: Adjusted EBITDA is expected to be approximately $550 million-$585 million. The 53rd week is expected to contribute approximately $11 million to adjusted EBITDA.
statements.speaker: Bryan Langley

street.gap_assumption: No target year, so the gap uses the last consensus year, FY2030 (837.8M / 6,598.9M = 12.70%), against a 15% reading of 'mid-teens', same metric. Fiscal year ends late December, so Baba FY labels equal company fiscal years. Against FY2028 (11.92%) the gap is 308 bps.

evidence_of_progress.note: Order is [Q1 2026, Q2 2026], as stated by the CFO: Q1 10.5% vs 11.2% (document_id 231), Q2 12.2% vs 12.4% (document_id 112140), with about 110 bps of Q2 SG&A deleverage from one-time IEEPA tariff refund costs. Comps -3.7% Q1 and -2.1% Q2; existing home sales near 4 million annualized. Store-level margin is intact (stores 5+ years old at about 23% EBITDA per the CFO, Q2 FY2025), so the gap is deleverage from new stores and weak comps, not broken unit economics.

verdict: Closest structural match so far: new external CEO, a standing mid-teens EBITDA goal about 230 bps above consensus and stabilized estimates, but the goal is inherited, undated and tied to a housing recovery.
open_questions: Will Paulsen restate or date the mid-teens goal as CEO (not found in Q1 or Q2 FY2026 calls), and is an Investor Day planned?
How much of the gap closes on housing turnover and comp leverage versus self-help (cost, merchandising system, slower store growth)?
Does slowing new store openings to fund buybacks lift reported margin mechanically by cutting pre-opening and young-store drag?
